Lantern 4.2

Released 21 October. Thank you to everyone who filed an issue.

Upgrading from 4.1

  1. Back up your lantern.toml.
  2. Install the new package and restart the service.
  3. Run lantern doctor; it lists any removed settings.
    • Settings marked removed must be deleted by hand.
    • Settings marked renamed are migrated for you.
  4. Check the dashboard once and confirm the version reads 4.2.0.

Highlights

  • new Saved searches can be shared by link.
  • new The activity feed groups repeated events, so a noisy night produces one line rather than two hundred.
  • fix Large imports no longer stall at 99 percent.
  • breaking The legacy /v1/events endpoint is removed.

4.2.0 21 October

Added

  • Shareable saved searches
    • Links expire after 30 days unless pinned.
      • Pinned links are listed under Settings → Sharing.
      • Revoking a link takes effect immediately.
    • Read-only by default.
  • Grouped activity feed, with a toggle to turn it off.
  • Keyboard shortcut g then s opens search.

Changed

  1. Default page size is now 50 instead of 25.
  2. Timestamps use the viewer's time zone.
  3. The sidebar remembers whether it was collapsed.

Fixed

  • Imports of more than 100,000 rows stalled at 99 percent.
  • Dates before 1970 were shown as blank.
  • A crash when a saved search had no name.

4.1.3 2 October

Security

Session tokens are now rotated on password change. Existing sessions are signed out once.

Fixed

  • Export to CSV quoted fields incorrectly when they contained a line break.
  • The “Back” link on the settings page returned to the wrong screen.

Deprecations

--legacy-auth
Will be removed in 5.0. Use token authentication instead.
/v1/events
Already removed in this release; see the highlights above.
feed.group_window
Accepts seconds only. Duration strings such as "5m" will be accepted from 4.3.

Known issues

  1. Grouped feed entries may show the earliest rather than the latest time until refreshed.
  2. Shared links opened in a private window ask for a second sign-in.
  3. Very long search names are cut off in the sidebar.
